newsitem.title: GERMANY: Frankfurt says 7 pct of banks quit city in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Frankfurt says 7 pct of banks quit city in 1996.

text.p: Frankfurt, the German financial capital struggling to keep up with rival centres like London, sustained a seven percent drop in the number of banks in the city last year, mainly because several foreign banks closed representative offices.
Frankfurt's Chamber of Commerce said on Thursday the number of banks in Frankfurt fell to 392 from 422 in 1996 after having remained broadly stable in 1995.
The Chamber said it was too early to tell if a trend towards fewer foreign banks was developing.
The closures were mainly by less prominent banks that did not do business in the city and had only been represented here to gather information or for reasons of prestige, it said.
"If it does become a trend, that would not exactly be positive for the international character of our financial centre," said Dieter Schwab, head of the Chamber's banking and insurance department.
"But I don't think the decline reduces the importance of Germany's financial centre."

Frankfurt has been paranoid about losing out to financial capitals like London ever since major domestic banks like Deutsche Bank AG and Dresdner Bank AG embarked on a foreign acquisition spree, locating much of their investment banking business in London.
But over the past three year regulators have done much to relax market restrictions here and reform the stock and debt markets to meet international standards.
The changes are having some effect.

Deutsche and Commerzbank AG said last week they would soon repatriate mark-denominated securities repurchase business to Frankfurt from London in response to the Bundesbank's move to relax stringent requirements on such "repo" activities.

The Chamber of Commerce attributed the decline in bank numbers to the closure of representative office, mergers by foreign banks, organisational streamlining and increased use of international communications systems which made a local presence unnecessary.
The number of German banks in the city was largely stable, falling to 144 from 145. Foreign banks in the city fell to 248 from 277.
